definitions.title: Three Natural-Domain Restrictions
definitions.statement: When a function is given by a formula, exclude inputs that make an even root negative or a denominator (or a denominator's root) zero; everything else is allowed.
conditions: Combine restrictions with intersection, one restriction at a time
definitions.explanation: Nearly every domain exercise in this set is solved by scanning the formula for fractions and square roots and writing down the forbidden values. Even powers like x^(2/3) impose no restriction because the cube root accepts all real numbers.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Read the formula left to right and collect the restrictions; the domain is what survives.

definitions.title: Difference Quotient
definitions.statement: The difference quotient measures the average rate of change of f over an interval of length h; simplifying it is the algebraic precursor to the derivative.
conditions: h must be nonzero before canceling
For sqrt functions, rationalize the numerator
definitions.explanation: Substitute x+h everywhere, expand carefully, subtract f(x), then factor h out of every remaining term and cancel. The h that cancels is exactly why the expression stays finite as h shrinks.
definitions.keyTakeaway: If h does not cancel from the denominator, an algebra mistake was made.

definitions.title: Even/Odd Algebraic Test
definitions.statement: Replace x by -x throughout the formula: if the expression is unchanged the function is even (y-axis symmetry); if every term flips sign it is odd (origin symmetry).
conditions: A single mixed term like x^2 + x defeats both tests
Domain must itself be symmetric about 0
definitions.explanation: Powers tell the story instantly for polynomials: only even powers means even, only odd powers means odd, a mixture means neither. Products inherit parity the way signs multiply.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Parity is decided term by term — one wrong power spoils both symmetries.

definitions.title: Standard Graph Transformations
definitions.statement: Vertical changes (outside the function argument) act as written; horizontal changes (inside the argument) act opposite to what the sign suggests.
conditions: Reflections and shifts do not commute in general
definitions.explanation: The most common error is reading f(x+3) as a shift right. Inside the argument, + moves left because the input must be 3 smaller to reach the same value.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Outside behaves honestly; inside behaves oppositely.

definitions.title: Domain of a Composition
definitions.statement: The domain of f(g(x)) consists of the inputs x that g accepts AND whose outputs g(x) the outer function f also accepts.
conditions: Always impose restrictions before simplifying the composed formula
definitions.explanation: Simplifying first can erase visible warnings: for f = sqrt and g = 1/(x-1) the composition equals sqrt(1/(x-1)), and the fraction must be nonnegative, which forces x > 1, not merely x different from 1.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Restrict first, simplify second — the domain is decided before the algebra.
